meta.title: He Couldn't Afford a Patent, So He Gave Away Half of Blue Jeans
meta.hook: A tailor who couldn't afford a patent fee co-invented blue jeans.
meta.description: In 1872, tailor Jacob Davis had been reinforcing work pants with copper rivets to stop the pockets tearing, but couldn't afford the patent filing fee. He offered fabric supplier Levi Strauss half the patent if Strauss paid the cost. On May 20, 1873, the two were granted US patent #139121 for riveted work pants — the design that became the Levi's 501.

scenes.narration: In eighteen seventy-two, a tailor named Jacob Davis couldn't afford the paperwork for his own invention.

scenes.narration: That patent became the Levi's five-oh-one, a design built for miners that's stayed largely unchanged for over a century and a half.
